name: Record Atlas variant-identity clusters (candidate rule)
note: NOT WIRED INTO THE SITE. This is the rule and the number it produces, written up in docs/variant-clusters.md, for review before any surname page changes. A cluster here is a connected component of surnames.json's variant graph, restricted to `spelling` and `grammar` edges only -- `curated` (Wikidata's `said to be the same as`) and `sounds` are never allowed to SEED a merge, because both were found, on this data, to chain into false identity claims (Wikidata's P460 links cross-dialect/cross-script CJK romanizations as freely as genuine spelling variants; `sounds` chains exactly as the brief describes). Every accepted edge additionally passed: (1) a length-scaled bounded edit distance on the folded, separator-stripped spelling -- max(1, min(3, shorter_name_len // 4)); (2) a minimum stripped length of 5, since short names have too little content for edit distance to mean anything (Cook/Zook is one edit apart and NOT the same family); (3) co-attestation in a country NOT among the six largest, most complete registers (BE, DK, FR, PL, US, ES) unless the attestation there is `archive` tier -- a shared country among those six is not corroboration, because almost any plausible short string appears in them by base rate (Hasan/Hazan share BE/DK/ES/FR/PL/US and are NOT the same name). Components larger than 9 members are rejected outright (1 of them, 10 names, in this build). Country pooling additionally stops at 3 hops within an accepted cluster, even though the cluster itself may be smaller: a short chain of individually-verified edges can still walk further than any one edge should be trusted to carry. Every pooled country on a member carries `via` (which other member attests it), `how` (that member's own evidence tier for the country), `hops` (distance within THIS verified cluster, never the raw variant graph), and `link` (the edge kinds on each hop of the path an identity claim would have to be taken on).
